title: One script, many targets
story: You have {{ntarget}} targets in inputs/, target_1.pdb to target_{{ntarget}}.pdb. mpnn_array.sh uses $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to pick one. Submit it as a job array with one task per target.

lesson.title: One request, many jobs

parts.note: ...5 copies of the script, numbered 1 to 5. Each one is its own job with its own GPU and memory, from the script's `#SBATCH` lines.
Inside, `$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID` is that copy's number, so each picks a different input.

lesson.why: Slurm runs as many copies at once as there are free GPUs, and queues the rest.

files.~/{{project}}/mpnn_array.sh:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=mpnn_arr
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --output=slurm-%j.out

module load anaconda
conda activate proteinmpnn

python /opt/ProteinMPNN/protein_mpnn_run.py \
  --pdb_path inputs/target_${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}.pdb \
  --out_folder outputs/target_${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}

jobRules.log:
Designing 8 sequences for inputs/target_{{task}}.pdb
Job finished

tasks.text: Submit mpnn_array.sh as an array of {{ntarget}} tasks
Wait until every task has written its outputs

hints: `--array=1-N` makes N copies of the job, numbered 1 to N. Add it on the command line or as an #SBATCH line.
